cards.html: When a service won't start or keeps dying, the same four steps solve almost every case: read the state, read the logs, decode the exit status, and reproduce the start by hand in the service's exact conditions. This chapter is a checklist you can follow under pressure, plus a table of the failures you will meet most often.

1. State: systemctl status levelup. Look at Active, the code= and status= on the "Main PID" or "Process" line, and the last log lines.
  2. Logs: journalctl -u levelup -b -n 100 --no-pager, or journalctl -xe right after a failure. Read upwards from systemd's "Failed" line to the first error your app printed.
  3. Decode: systemctl show levelup -p Result,ExecMainCode,ExecMainStatus. Result= is one of success, exit-code, signal, timeout, core-dump, watchdog, oom-kill or start-limit-hit.
  4. Reproduce as the service user, in its directory, with its environment, not as yourself in your shell:
sudo -u levelup env -i PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
  bash -c 'cd /opt/levelup/server_fastapi && .venv/bin/uvicorn main:app --port 8766'

env -i starts from an empty environment, as systemd does, so missing variables and PATH problems show up here too.

Two more tools: systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/levelup.service catches typos and unknown options in a unit file, and systemctl cat levelup shows the unit as systemd actually sees it, drop-ins included.

SymptomLikely causeFix
status=203/EXECExecStart path wrong, file not executable, bad shebang, or script lacks chmod +xCheck the path with ls -l; use an absolute path to the venv's binary
status=200/CHDIRWorkingDirectory= doesn't exist, or the user can't enter itCreate it; fix ownership and permissions
status=217/USERUser= names an account that doesn't existCreate the user, or fix the name
status=226/NAMESPACEA sandboxing path (for example in ReadWritePaths=) doesn't existCreate the directory, or use StateDirectory=
status=1/FAILUREThe app itself exited with an errorRead its traceback in the journal
code=killed, status=9/KILLOut-of-memory kill (MemoryMax= or system OOM), or it ignored SIGTERM until TimeoutStopSec=journalctl -k for OOM; handle SIGTERM in the app
Result: start-limit-hitIt crashed too often within StartLimitIntervalSec=Fix the cause, then systemctl reset-failed levelup and start it

SymptomLikely causeFix
activating (auto-restart) foreverIt starts and crashes in a loopRead the first error in the logs; it repeats every cycle
"Address already in use"Another process holds the port, maybe a copy you started by handsudo ss -ltnp 'sport = :8766' to find it
"Permission denied" or "Read-only file system"File ownership, or ProtectSystem= / ProtectHome=chown the data directory; add ReadWritePaths=
ModuleNotFoundErrorWrong Python: the system one instead of the venv'sPoint ExecStart= at .venv/bin/…
Works in the terminal, fails as a serviceEnvironment: PATH, API keys, HOMEEnvironmentFile=; absolute paths
Edits have no effectForgot daemon-reload, or edited a file systemd isn't usingsystemctl cat to see the file in use
Unit levelup.service not foundWrong name, or the file is in the wrong folder or lacks .servicels /etc/systemd/system/
Timer never runsYou enabled the service instead of the timersystemctl enable --now x.timer; check list-timers

1. sudo supervisorctl status shows the state: FATAL, BACKOFF or EXITED.
  2. sudo supervisorctl tail levelup stderr (or stdout with redirect_stderr) shows the app's own output.
  3. /var/log/supervisor/supervisord.log shows Supervisor's view: spawn errors, "exited: … (exit status 1; not expected)", "gave up: … entered FATAL state, too many start retries too quickly".
  4. Reproduce with sudo -u levelup env -i …, as above.

SymptomLikely causeFix
FATAL Exited too quickly (process log may have details)It crashes within startsecs on every tryRead the program log; fix the crash
spawn error / "can't find command"command path wrong, or not executableAbsolute path to the binary
ERROR (no such process)The new program was never loadedsupervisorctl reread then update
unix:///var/run/supervisor.sock no such filesupervisord isn't runningsudo systemctl start supervisor
Edits to .conf have no effectYou ran restart instead of reread + updatereread, then update
Workers keep running after a stopChildren weren't signalledstopasgroup=true, killasgroup=true
App can't find HOME or its configuser= doesn't set environment variablesenvironment=HOME="/opt/levelup",…

cards.s: Questions that find the cause fast
cards.html:
• What changed? A deploy, a package upgrade, an edited config, a full disk (df -h), an expired certificate?
  • Does it fail at start, after a fixed time, or under load? Start-up failures are config; failures after a fixed time are memory or timeouts; failures under load are limits (file descriptors, tasks, memory).
  • Is it the same error each restart? Read the first one, not the last one.

cards.s: Lab: break it five ways (VM, free)
cards.html:
For each step, break the demo unit, run daemon-reload and restart, diagnose with the four steps, write down the status you saw, then fix it:

  1. Point ExecStart at a file that doesn't exist.
  2. Set User=nobodyhere.
  3. Set WorkingDirectory=/opt/missing.
  4. Make the app read os.environ["API_KEY"] at start-up and don't provide it. Watch it loop, then hit start-limit-hit. Recover with reset-failed.
  5. Start a second copy by hand on port 8000, then restart the service: "Address already in use".

Repeat steps 1 and 4 under Supervisor and compare what status and the logs show.

1. What does status=203/EXEC usually mean?
  2. Your service shows start-limit-hit. You fixed the bug. What must you run before it will start again?
  3. Which command shows the unit file systemd is really using, drop-ins included?
  4. Why reproduce with sudo -u <user> env -i … rather than just running the command?
  5. Supervisor says ERROR (no such process) for a program you just added. What did you skip?

Answers. 1: The program couldn't be executed: wrong path, not executable, or a bad shebang. 2: systemctl reset-failed <unit> (then start it). 3: systemctl cat <unit>. 4: It reproduces the service's user and empty environment, which is where most "works for me" failures come from. 5: supervisorctl reread and update.
